source: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center: guide maps (2023 and 2022)

artworks.title: The Gathering Space
artworks.description: Begin your tour on the entry floor (Level 3), in the Gathering Space, near the gift shop. The tall hall is walled in glass.
artworks.galleryName: The Gathering Space
artworks.placeNote: Number 1 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: The ramp to the exhibits
artworks.description: Take the ramp or the elevator on the far side of the Gathering Space to start your exhibit tour on Level 2. The exhibits run as a timeline, from 18,000 years ago to the present day.
artworks.galleryName: The Gathering Space
artworks.placeNote: Number 2 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Observation Tower
artworks.description: Don’t forget to visit the observation tower! Its elevator is by the main entrance.
artworks.galleryName: The Gathering Space
artworks.placeNote: Where the museum’s guide map puts it.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Museum Gift Shop
artworks.description: From Pendleton blankets, pottery and craft supplies to handmade birch baskets, jewelry, textiles and locally harvested maple syrup: the shop sells work made by certified Native American artists.
artworks.galleryName: Museum Gift Shop
artworks.placeNote: Where the museum’s guide map puts it.

artworks.title: Introduction
artworks.description: At the bottom of the ramp, turn left into the exhibits. A large colour photo of today’s tribal members and an interactive, glass-enclosed tabletop model of the reservation introduce Pequot life from centuries past to the present.
artworks.galleryName: Exhibit Entrance: the introduction, a scale model of the reservation and tribal life today
artworks.placeNote: Number 3 (2023) · 1 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: The Glacier
artworks.description: Travel through a glacial crevasse in New England during the Ice Age. The escalator takes you down to Level 1.
artworks.galleryName: The Glacier: the escalator down through a glacial crevasse to Level 1
artworks.placeNote: Number 2 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: The World of Ice
artworks.description: The centrepiece of this exhibit is a revolving globe showing the advance and retreat of the Wisconsin Glacier.
artworks.galleryName: World of Ice and the Arrival of the People; the escalator from Level 2 arrives here
artworks.placeNote: Number 4 (2023) · 3 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. The 2023 guide puts the World of Ice on Level 1, by the escalator from Level 2 (the 2022 guide had it on Level 2).
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Arrival of the People Gallery
artworks.description: The works of nine Native artists represent the creation stories of each artist’s tribe.
artworks.galleryName: World of Ice and the Arrival of the People; the escalator from Level 2 arrives here
artworks.placeNote: Number 4 (2023) · 4 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. The 2023 guide puts the Native art and creation stories with the World of Ice on Level 1.

artworks.title: Arrival of the People Theater
artworks.description: Storytellers relate creation stories in English and in their own languages (a short film).
artworks.galleryName: World of Ice and the Arrival of the People; the escalator from Level 2 arrives here
artworks.placeNote: Number 4 (2023) · 5 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. The 2023 guide puts the storytellers’ film with the World of Ice on Level 1.

artworks.title: Life in a Cold Climate
artworks.description: Exhibits on large animals that once roamed New England, like the mastodon, the giant beaver and dire wolves.
artworks.galleryName: Life in a Cold Climate: Ice Age animals and the caribou hunt
artworks.placeNote: Number 5 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Caribou Hunt Diorama
artworks.description: A life-size re-creation of a caribou hunt 11,000 years ago: discover how family members took part.
artworks.galleryName: Life in a Cold Climate: Ice Age animals and the caribou hunt
artworks.placeNote: Number 6 (2023) · 6 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: The Changing Environment
artworks.description: A life-size diorama and touch-screen computers detail the forest habitat of Connecticut, and show how scientists learned how this area changed over the past 15,000 years.
artworks.galleryName: World of Ice and the Arrival of the People; the escalator from Level 2 arrives here
artworks.placeNote: Number 7 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: The Four Seasons
artworks.description: Dioramas portray life at Mashantucket from 8,000 to 3,000 years ago, season by season, with ancient tools.
artworks.galleryName: The Four Seasons and the Three Sisters; pick up the audio tour here
artworks.placeNote: Number 8 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Tool Theater
artworks.description: A short film on making and using stone tools: the actual tools used by the Mashantucket Pequots for farming and building.
artworks.galleryName: Tool Theater
artworks.placeNote: Number 8 (2023) · 9 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Introduction to Horticulture: the Three Sisters
artworks.description: A life-size diorama of growing corn, beans and squash, which Natives call the “Three Sisters”. Pick up an audio guide here before you enter the village, and dial the numbers on the floor to hear each scene explained.
artworks.galleryName: The Four Seasons and the Three Sisters; pick up the audio tour here
artworks.placeNote: Number 9 (2023) · 10, 11 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: 16th-Century Pequot Village
artworks.description: Walk through a life-size Pequot village and imagine life before the arrival of Europeans: a realistic coastal and woodland setting of the 1500s, with wigwams, people at work and the sounds of the village.
artworks.galleryName: 16th-Century Pequot Village
artworks.placeNote: Number 10 (2023) · 12 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center, via Google Arts & Culture

artworks.title: Pequot Daily Life Gallery
artworks.description: Once in the village, notice the side galleries: videos of Native artisans making the tools and utensils of everyday life in southeastern Connecticut 450 years ago.
artworks.galleryName: Pequot Daily Life Gallery (a side gallery of the village)
artworks.placeNote: Number 10 (2023) · 13 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Pequot Society Gallery
artworks.description: Learn about the Tribe’s social and political organization, ceremonies, spirituality and medicine.
artworks.galleryName: Pequot Society Gallery (a side gallery of the village)
artworks.placeNote: Number 14 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Arrival of the Europeans Gallery
artworks.description: The political, economic and religious reasons that led to the arrival of the English and the Dutch.
artworks.galleryName: Palisaded fort and the way out of the village: the Arrival of the Europeans
artworks.placeNote: Number 15 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. Where the 2022 guide puts it, on the way out of the village (approximate).

artworks.title: Palisaded Fort
artworks.description: A ring of tall posts around part of the village: the kind of fort the Pequots built in the 1600s.
artworks.galleryName: Palisaded fort and the way out of the village: the Arrival of the Europeans
artworks.placeNote: Where the museum’s guide map puts it.

artworks.title: Prelude to War
artworks.description: Leaving the village, enter the Clash of Cultures exhibits: video displays tell how trading conflicts led to tension between the Pequots, the English and the Dutch.
artworks.galleryName: Clash of Cultures: the Pequot War of 1636-1637
artworks.placeNote: Number 11 (2023) · 16 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Wampum Theater
artworks.description: Learn about the tube-shell beads first used for ceremonial purposes and then for trade.
artworks.galleryName: Clash of Cultures: the Pequot War of 1636-1637
artworks.placeNote: Number 17 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. Next to War Theater 1 in the 2022 guide.

artworks.title: The Massacre at Mystic
artworks.description: How, in 1637, the colonies of Connecticut and Massachusetts attacked the fort at Mystic, killing about 600 Pequots.
artworks.galleryName: Clash of Cultures: the Pequot War of 1636-1637
artworks.placeNote: Number 18 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: The Witness
artworks.description: A dramatic half-hour film about the 1637 Pequot War, seen through the eyes of a Pequot elder who survived the Massacre at Mystic (for ages 12 and older). Viewings at 11 AM, 1 PM and 3 PM.
artworks.galleryName: War Theater 2: The Witness (film)
artworks.placeNote: Number 11 (2023) · 19 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. The 2023 guide map points The Witness to War Theaters 1 and 2.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Life on the Reservation
artworks.description: Take the escalator to Level 2, and discover what life on and off the reservation meant for Pequot families.
artworks.galleryName: Life on the Reservation: Robin Cassacinamon, the Fort at Mashantucket, and the door out to the 1780 Farmstead
artworks.placeNote: Number 12 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Robin Cassacinamon
artworks.description: Meet the Pequot sachem (1645–1692) who helped the Pequots return to their land.
artworks.galleryName: Life on the Reservation: Robin Cassacinamon, the Fort at Mashantucket, and the door out to the 1780 Farmstead
artworks.placeNote: Number 20 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Explore the Fort at Mashantucket
artworks.description: An interactive program to move through a 3D computer model of the fort that archaeologists discovered on this site in 1992.
artworks.galleryName: Life on the Reservation: Robin Cassacinamon, the Fort at Mashantucket, and the door out to the 1780 Farmstead
artworks.placeNote: Number 21 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: 1780 Farmstead
artworks.description: Step inside a typical farmstead. In warm weather, tour the two-acre garden outside (the door at the top of the map).
artworks.galleryName: Life on the Reservation: Robin Cassacinamon, the Fort at Mashantucket, and the door out to the 1780 Farmstead
artworks.placeNote: Number 22 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Meeting House Mini-Theater: Our Remembered Sisters
artworks.description: Our Remembered Sisters describes the lives of three Mashantucket women in the first half of the 19th century.
artworks.galleryName: Meeting House Mini-Theater
artworks.placeNote: Number 23 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: The Changing Reservation
artworks.description: A computer interactive shows how the shape and nature of Pequot land changed over the last 300 years.
artworks.galleryName: The Changing Reservation
artworks.placeNote: Number 24 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.

artworks.title: Federal Recognition Theater: Bringing The People Home
artworks.description: The film Bringing The People Home tells how the Tribe achieved federal recognition in 1983.
artworks.galleryName: Federal Recognition Theater and the galleries around the two round exhibit rooms (where the theater is exactly is approximate)
artworks.placeNote: Number 25 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps. Approximate: between the two round exhibit rooms, where the 2022 guide puts it.

artworks.title: Tribal Portrait Gallery
artworks.description: Photos of present-day members of the Mashantucket Pequot Tribal Nation; listen to their voices as they recount what it means to be a Pequot and Native American.
artworks.galleryName: Tribal Portrait Gallery
artworks.placeNote: Number 13 (2023) · 26 (2022) on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)

artworks.title: Mashantucket Gallery
artworks.description: Exit the Portrait Gallery and walk straight ahead to the Mashantucket Gallery, where changing exhibitions highlight Native art and culture. Then turn right, go through the double doors, cross the auditorium lobby and take the ramp back up to the Gathering Space.
artworks.galleryName: Mashantucket Gallery: changing exhibitions of Native art and culture
artworks.placeNote: Number 14, 15 on the museum’s guide maps.
artworks.imageCredit: Mashantucket Pequot Museum & Research Center (museum guide map, 2023)
